criteria.criterion: Use Serde crate landing page on crates.io
criteria.description: Navigate to and use the Serde crate landing page on crates.io (e.g., https://crates.io/crates/serde) as the sole intended source. Full credit if the agent attempts to load the landing page and clearly bases results on it, OR if access is prevented by an external blocker (CAPTCHA, outage, region block, JS not loading) and the agent clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent’s attempt is unclear or it uses other sources despite the landing-page being accessible. No credit if it makes no attempt to access crates.io and instead relies on other sources without justification.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows the agent was on https://crates.io/crates/serde and scrolled twice on that page. Screenshot 1 explicitly shows the crates.io Serde landing page header area with “serde v1.0.229”. Screenshots 2 and 3 show crates.io-style sections consistent with the same crate page.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Evidence supports that the agent used the Serde crate landing page on crates.io as required.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the crates.io website with the header/logo “crates.io” and the crate page title area reading “serde v1.0.229” with the description “A generic serialization/deserialization framework”. Tabs like “Readme”, “Code”, “316 Versions”, “Dependencies”, “Dependents”, and “Security” are visible, indicating this is the Serde crate landing page on crates.io.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Satisfied. The screenshot clearly shows the Serde crate landing page on crates.io and the agent’s predicted output states it used that landing page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None for source usage; the screenshot supports being on the correct crates.io crate landing page.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the crates.io page layout for the Serde crate: a code example on the left and a right-hand sidebar with headings and links including “Homepage” (showing “serde.rs”), “Documentation” (showing “docs.rs/serde/1.0.229”), “Repository” (showing “github.com/serde-rs/serde”), “Owners”, and “Categories”. This is consistent with a crate landing page view on crates.io.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The visible UI elements (crate sidebar with Homepage/Documentation/Repository/Owners/Categories) indicate the agent is using the Serde crate landing page on crates.io as required. No evidence suggests use of other sources in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output includes many metadata/statistics fields (latest version, release date, min Rust version, license, package size, downloads, versions count) that are not visible in this screenshot; however, Criterion 0 only checks that the Serde crate landing page on crates.io is used, which is supported by the screenshot.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a crates.io-style page section titled “Stats Overview” with large metrics and a chart labeled “Downloads over the last 90 days,” plus a footer area with links like “Rust” and “rust-lang/crates.io.” However, the screenshot does not show the page header, URL bar, or the crate title/name “serde,” so the specific crate landing page cannot be confirmed from pixels alone.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial support. The visible UI strongly resembles the crates.io crate stats section, but the screenshot alone does not explicitly confirm it is the Serde crate landing page (no visible “serde” identifier or URL). The agent’s predicted output asserts it used https://crates.io/crates/serde; that is plausible but not directly verifiable from this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims to be on the Serde crate landing page and references “serde v1.0.229” in the heading, but the screenshot does not show any crate heading or name—only the stats section and chart.
